source_passages: Home All News Inspiring ‘Autos for Love’ Owners Delight in Giving Away Cars to Needy Neighbors Cathy and Dane Bailey from Auto Experts of Colleyville – credit, Autos for Love Once a year, the owners of a Texas auto-repair shop would refurbish a donated car and then hand the keys to a member of their community in need.
Autos for Love started years ago when the Baileys, who own Auto Experts of Colleyville, wanted to try and put in a little more elbow grease on behalf of those who have no wheels to grease.
Refurbishing gently used cars donated by community members, their aim was to give away one per year.

source_passages: This year, the Baileys began looking for who in town needed them the most, and some residents called in to nominate their friend Barbara Farison, a mother whose car was totaled by another motorist running a red light.
Unable to secure a replacement, Farison and her kids have walked everywhere for 3 years when alternative transportation wasn’t available, including to school and to buy groceries.
It has exposed them to toil, the elements, and in Farison’s case, to an incident of violent crime she only narrowly avoided.

positive_change.result: Les communautés pastorales du Ladakh ont réduit les pertes de bétail dues aux léopards des neiges en renforçant les enclos et en développant des activités économiques alternatives.
positive_change.beneficiaries: Les éleveurs et villageois de 45 villages de Ladakh vivant en coexistence avec les léopards des neiges.

fact_checks.sentence: À Ladakh, l’association Snow Leopard Conservancy accompagne 45 villages pour diminuer les attaques des léopards des neiges sur les troupeaux.
source_passages: Credit: Minh Cong Pham / Shutterstock Twenty years ago, villagers might have retaliated by killing the snow leopard, which is listed as vulnerable on the International Union for Conservation of Nature’s red list of threatened species.
“These happened often when I was young,” says Tsewang Namgail, who heads the Ladakh-based Snow Leopard Conservancy – India Trust (SLC-IT).

His childhood experience helped Namgail to realize that simply compensating local communities for livestock losses was not enough: “We had to somehow make villages near snow leopard habitats more disposed towards protecting them,” he says.
Today, the Trust works with Ladakh’s livestock-owning communities in 45 villages to reduce the costs of living alongside snow leopards.

positive_change.result: La tapisserie de Bayeux, un monument historique brodé au XIe siècle, est désormais reconnu et protégé comme patrimoine mondial par l'Unesco, ce qui assure sa préservation et sa valorisation.
positive_change.beneficiaries: Les visiteurs, chercheurs, et l'ensemble du patrimoine culturel français et mondial bénéficient de cette reconnaissance et conservation.

fact_checks.sentence: La tapisserie de Bayeux est une broderie réalisée au XIe siècle, représentant près de 623 personnages et de multiples scènes historiques.
source_passages: La tapisserie de Bayeux ou broderie de Bayeux, successivement désignée « Telle du Conquest » (« toile de la Conquête ») par les chanoines de la cathédrale Notre-Dame de Bayeux, toilette de la Saint-Jean et toilette du duc Guillaume au XVIIIe siècle, ou encore tapisserie de la reine Mathilde au XIXe siècle, est une broderie (anciennement « tapisserie aux points d'aiguille ») du XIe siècle inscrite depuis 2007 au registre international Mémoire du monde par l'Unesco.
